# ISBN diagnosis

Checked November 4, 2026. No CSV values were edited and nothing was imported into a database.

## Source and method

Downloaded [Goodbooks-10k books.csv](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/zygmuntz/goodbooks-10k/master/books.csv) again into memory and compared it byte for byte with the existing week3 copy. They are identical, so the existing file was retained rather than overwritten. Both file hashes were checked again after this report was generated.

Every data record in both files was parsed with Python’s CSV reader, keeping identifiers as text. The appendix gives the original values and diagnosis for every row. “Row” means CSV record number including the header as row 1, not a physical line number if a quoted field contains a newline.

ISBN-10 requires nine digits followed by a digit or uppercase X (meaning 10); its weighted sum with weights 10 through 1 must be divisible by 11. ISBN-13 requires 13 digits, a book prefix 978 or 979 (not 9790), and an alternating 1/3 weighted sum divisible by 10. Historical ISBN-10s remain useful for this exercise. Valid here means structurally and mathematically valid, not proof of publisher allocation, registration-group validity, or a match to the title/edition.

The primary categories are mutually exclusive per column and sum to the record count. Blanks are counted separately. Presentation variants and scientific notation do not pass the strict “as written” check; possible interpretations are tested only in memory. ISBNs may legitimately be printed with separators. No correction is being recommended or performed. An ISBN-13 in the isbn column can be a valid identifier but is flagged separately as a column-format inconsistency.

Sources: [International ISBN Agency: What is an ISBN?](https://www.isbn-international.org/content/what-isbn/10), [ISBN.org: check digit and general questions](https://www.isbn.org/faqs_general_questions), [International ISBN Agency manual](https://www.isbn-international.org/sites/default/files/ISBN%20Manual%202012%20-corr.pdf).

## books.csv

10,000 records; two ISBN fields checked per record. SHA-256: `4d21d0e0433128657c752e3a3d0405ac0ec11675d6c70c64cb0abf4ab1acb76a`.

### isbn

| Diagnosis | Rows | Example (CSV row, book_id, raw value) | What it means / probable cause |
|---|---:|---|---|
| Short ISBN-10; zero-padding passes | 6,587 | Row 2, book_id 1: <code>439023483</code>; hypothetical padded form: 0439023483 | Consistent with leading zeros removed by numeric conversion. Hypothetical left-padding to 10 characters passes, but this does not prove the intended identifier. |
| Valid as written | 2,690 | Row 10, book_id 9: <code>1416524797</code>; ISBN-10 | Passes length, allowed-character, prefix (ISBN-13), and checksum tests. Assignment to this title is not verified. |
| Missing | 700 | Row 107, book_id 106: (blank); blank | No identifier supplied or lost upstream; a blank is missing data, not a checksum failure. |
| Wrong length | 14 | Row 917, book_id 916: <code>812971060</code>; 9 characters | Possible truncated/extra digits or an identifier of another type. Its length is not an ISBN-10 or ISBN-13 length. |
| Bad checksum | 9 | Row 1444, book_id 1443: <code>9380658797</code>; checksum fails | Length and characters fit, but the check digit calculation fails. Possible mistyped digits, truncation/rounding, or incorrect source metadata. |

### isbn13

| Diagnosis | Rows | Example (CSV row, book_id, raw value) | What it means / probable cause |
|---|---:|---|---|
| Scientific notation; expanded value fails | 8,454 | Row 2, book_id 1: <code>9.78043902348e+12</code>; exact expansion: 9780439023480 | Probably numeric export, possibly rounded/truncated. Exact decimal expansion fails validation. It cannot safely be accepted as an ISBN. |
| Scientific notation; expanded value passes | 956 | Row 3, book_id 2: <code>9.78043955493e+12</code>; exact expansion: 9780439554930 | Probably exported as a number. The literal is not an ISBN string; exact decimal expansion passes the checksum. No file was repaired. |
| Missing | 585 | Row 107, book_id 106: (blank); blank | No identifier supplied or lost upstream; a blank is missing data, not a checksum failure. |
| Decimal numeric notation | 5 | Row 959, book_id 958: <code>76783609419.0</code>; integer part: 76783609419; fails length/prefix/checksum validation | A trailing decimal fraction is not ISBN text and suggests floating-point export. The integer part is also checked below; removing .0 does not restore missing digits or establish a book identifier. |

### Checks across the two columns

Using only individually passing raw or diagnostic interpretations: **929 pairs agree**, **12 pairs conflict**, and **9,059 rows cannot be compared**. These diagnostic interpretations are not accepted repairs. A 978 ISBN-13 is compared with the ISBN-10 by converting its first nine digits and recomputing the check digit. A 979 ISBN-13 has no ISBN-10 equivalent.

Pair conflicts can indicate numeric rounding (including rounding that coincidentally passes a checksum), different editions, or a wrong identifier copied into one field; two passing checksums do not establish that both belong to the same book. Flags below overlap the primary counts.

## Interpretation and limits

The original delivery already contains numeric-looking identifier damage, so the problems did not necessarily originate with this assignment. Scientific notation and missing leading zeros are consistent with numeric conversion during an upstream export. Batch 2 also contains obvious malformed values and conflicting pairs. The files alone cannot establish which software or person caused any specific error. These are probable explanations, not a proven history.

A checksum can detect many transcription errors but cannot establish that a book exists or that an identifier is assigned to this title. Missing identifiers, duplicated records, and repeated ISBNs are not automatically invalid ISBNs; edition matching and deduplication are separate decisions. No values have been fixed, rejected from a database, or otherwise changed.
